summary.description: Man-made organic compounds containing tin, typically colourless to yellow liquids with a foul odour. Used as marine anti-fouling agents and wood preservatives.
emission_sources: Gradual release from products treated with TBTs
Use as fungicides in wood preservatives
environmental_impact: Endocrine disruption in animals due to hormone interference
Bioaccumulation in fish and other aquatic organisms
Persistent in soils and aquatic environments, with low mobility

top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: TBTs bioaccumulate in marine organisms and act as endocrine disruptors, leading to severe ecological imbalances in aquatic ecosystems.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: The use of TBTs in commercial products highlights the need for safer chemical practices and better waste management to reduce persistent environmental pollutants.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: TBTs can contaminate aquatic environments through leaching and runoff, affecting water quality and posing risks to aquatic organisms and dependent communities.
